title: The Fred Allen Show
paragraphs: Long-running topical comedy-variety vehicle for Fred Allen and Portland Hoffa under multiple historical titles. Frozen GRH container has 277 objects, including one undated/approximate item and one collector file dated June 29, 1949 despite the documented June 26 final broadcast.

GRH documents the program through Linit Bath Club Revue (October 23, 1932 to April 16, 1933), Salad Bowl Revue (August 4, 1933 to December 1, 1933), Sal Hepatica / Hour of Smiles transition (January 3, 1934 to July 4, 1934), and Town Hall Tonight (July 11, 1934 to September 27, 1939).

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Fred Allen (performer on 94 recordings and writer on 1 recording), Portland Hoffa (performer on 87 recordings), Minerva Pious (performer on 78 recordings), Al Goodman and His Orchestra (performer on 67 recordings), Kenny Delmar (performer on 62 recordings and announcer on 10 recordings), The De Marco Sisters (performer on 65 recordings), and Parker Fennelly (performer on 63 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network) and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include radio industry and broadcasting satire, music and performance, advertising, shopping and consumer culture, wartime and military life, topical news and current-events satire, and Hollywood and celebrity culture.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Topical satire in network radio comedy, American network comedy during World War II, and Postwar network comedy and emerging television competition.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|the-big-show|The Big Show]] (20 shared credited people), [[show|duffys-tavern|Duffy's Tavern]] (21 shared credited people), [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]] (19 shared credited people), [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]] (9 shared credited people), and [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]] (9 shared credited people).
